# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Geometric regularization, Depth-supervised NeRF, Geometric priors

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision refers to a family of regularization techniques that incorporate explicit geometric constraints—such as depth maps, 3D points, or structural priors—into the Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) training loop to resolve the shape-radiance ambiguity inherent in sparse-view or ill-posed reconstruction problems [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Unlike sibling methods that rely on semantic embeddings [11955-semantic-consistency-loss-clip-based.md] or diffusion priors [7381-diffusion-regularized-nerf.md], this family explicitly aligns the rendered density distribution or ray termination with external geometric signals, thereby accelerating convergence and suppressing artifacts like floaters in textureless regions [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the augmented loss structure defined by [Regularization and Loss Functions](8586-regularization-and-loss-functions.md):

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} + \sum_k \lambda_k \mathcal{L}_k $$

where $\mathcal{L}_k$ represents a geometric or depth-related regularization term [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The core mechanism involves computing a geometric signal (e.g., depth $D$, 3D point $\mathbf{X}$, or structural constraint) and comparing it against the differentiable volume rendering output. The rendering process computes the ray termination distribution $h(t) = T(t)\sigma(t)$, where $T(t)$ is the accumulated transmittance, allowing gradients to flow from geometric losses back to the density field $\sigma$ [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Common strategies include direct pixel-wise depth comparison [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md], distribution alignment via KL divergence [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md, 12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md], or enforcing multi-view consistency [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md].

## Subtopics

### [Geometric Baseline Regularization](7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md)
A composite loss designed to prevent degenerate "copying" solutions in few-view settings by enforcing foreground completeness, frustum consistency, and depth distribution compactness [7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md]. It differs from siblings by relying solely on internal volume rendering consistency without external depth priors [7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md].

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
Optimizes NeRF by dynamically adjusting the sampling interval $[t_n, t_f]$ along rays based on multi-view consistency errors of adapted monocular depth priors [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md]. It sets itself apart by avoiding explicit geometric loss terms in favor of guided sampling and post-filtering [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md].

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
Addresses single-panorama reconstruction by initializing geometry via deformable alignment of multiple perspective depth projections to a canonical depth map [8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md]. It differs from siblings by explicitly constructing this canonical map via optimization before training, rather than applying loss to raw estimates [8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md].

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
Accelerates optimization with sparse views by incorporating depth supervision from sparse 3D keypoints generated during Structure-from-Motion (SfM) preprocessing [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. It imposes a KL-divergence loss forcing the rendered ray termination distribution to match surface priors from these keypoints, distinct from dense depth methods or smoothness-only regularizers [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md].

### [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md)
Enforces continuity on rendered depth maps using external priors (e.g., DepthAnythingV2) by modeling structural consistency through k-nearest neighbor (KNN) relationships in depth space [9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md]. It tolerates minor variations via a boundary value while penalizing large discontinuities, effective in sparse-view scenarios [9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md].

### [Statistical Depth Refinement](10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md)
Mitigates artifacts from noisy stereo depth by identifying outliers in depth residuals and replacing them with smoother estimates from an underfitting model [10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md]. It leverages early-stage training smoothing to clean the supervision signal, unlike direct supervision which amplifies noise [10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md].

### [Novel View Regularization](10806-novel-view-regularization.md)
Mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity in sparse data by injecting synthetic rays from novel camera poses into the optimization loop [10806-novel-view-regularization.md]. It generates intermediate views to constrain the density field, reducing overfitting to observed views without external priors [10806-novel-view-regularization.md].

### [3D Point Supervision Loss](12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md)
Minimizes the distance between learned 3D points (backprojected from rendered depth) and ground-truth 3D points [12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md]. Unlike DS-NeRF which applies loss on depth values, this enforces global geometric connection, resulting in better pose registration in sparse regimes [12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md].

### [Generalized Ray Supervision](14127-generalized-ray-supervision.md)
Treats arbitrary rays (e.g., shadow rays) as sensors recording incoming radiance, extending supervision beyond camera rays [14127-generalized-ray-supervision.md]. It leverages the fact that each pixel acts as an independent sensor with defined 3D location and orientation to constrain the neural field [14127-generalized-ray-supervision.md].

### Coarse-Fine Consistency Loss
- **definition**: A loss function that enforces consistency between depth estimates of the coarse and fine NeRF models to prevent ineffective hierarchical sampling and blur [S1].
- **formula**: $\mathcal{L}_{cfc} = \mathbf{1}_{\{m_f=1\}} \odot \|z_c - \hat{\nabla}(z_f)\|^2 + \mathbf{1}_{\{m_c=1\}} \odot \|\hat{\nabla}(z_c) - z_f\|^2$, where $z_c$ and $z_f$ are coarse and fine depths, and $m_c/m_f$ are reliability masks determined by reprojection [S1].

### Zero-level set projection
- **definition**: Refines inaccurate median depth from a pre-trained NeRF, particularly at grazing view angles, by iteratively projecting points onto the zero level-set of the surface using TSDF values [S2].
- **step**: For each 3D point $p$ on the viewing ray, perform exactly 4 iterative gradient descent steps along the ray direction using the TSDF predicted value to update the point position [S2].
- **formula**: $p_{new} = p_{old} + \alpha \times \hat{t}$, where $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}] = \phi(p)$; $p$ is the current 3D point, $\alpha$ is a small constant step size, $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}]$ are the tangent, normal, and feature outputs from network $\phi$ evaluated at $p$ [S2].
- **parameter**: $\alpha$: Small constant controlling the step size of the gradient descent update. Value not specified in this section [S2].
- **pitfall**: Median depth from a pre-trained NeRF becomes inaccurate when the angle between the view direction and the surface is small (grazing angles) [S2].
- **usage**: Applied in NeRFMeshing as a preprocessing step to initialize the mesh geometry before training the SSAN model [S2].

### Robust Depth Loss
- **definition**: A loss function designed to address geometry error degradation in extrapolation performance by being less sensitive to outliers than L2 loss, encouraging NeRF to terminate rays around pseudo depth while retaining freedom for inaccurate geometry [S3].
- **formula**: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{robust}}(\mathbf{r}) = \begin{cases} 0.5\Delta D(\mathbf{r})^{2}, &\text{if } \Delta D(\mathbf{r}) < \beta \\ \beta^{2} (0.5 + \log (\frac{\Delta D(\mathbf{r})}{\beta })), &\text{otherwise } \end{cases}$ where $\Delta D(\mathbf{r}) = \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) - D(\mathbf{r})$ is the absolute depth difference, $\beta$ is a constant set to 0.1, and $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ is the depth expectation along the camera axis of ray $r(t)$ [S3].
- **parameter**: $\beta$: A constant threshold for the robust depth loss, set to 0.1 throughout the experiments [S3].

### Depth Supervision with Planar Architectural Depth Priors
- **definition**: Incorporates precomputed depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls into NeRF training to enforce geometric constraints on textureless planar surfaces [S4].
- **step**: 1. Compute depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls using semantic segmentation. 2. Incorporate these priors into training with MSE and BoundL losses alongside photometric loss. 3. Train until convergence [S4].
- **parameter**: $\delta$ (BoundL tolerance): 1 mm. $\lambda_{color}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room). $\lambda_{depth}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room) [S4].
- **number**: RMSE of priors vs ground truth: 2.786 mm (bedroom), 3.201 mm (living room). Converged in 120,000 iterations [S4].
- **comparison**: Faster convergence than photometric-only (120k vs 200k) and patch-regularization (120k vs 280k) methods due to depth supervision enabling quick identification of empty spaces, concentrating sampling on occupied regions, and providing a stronger optimization signal [S4].

### Indirect Depth Supervision (KL Loss)
- **definition**: A regularization technique that uses depth priors to constrain the NeRF weights by aligning the probability distribution of rendering weights with the depth prior, specifically using KL divergence [S5].
- **formula**: $L_{KL} = \sum_{i}^{N_r} \sum_{t=t_n}^{t_f} D(r_i) - \epsilon \log w_k \exp(-\frac{(t - D(r_i))^2}{2\hat{\sigma}^2}) \Delta t_k$, where $w_k$ are rendering weights, $t_k$ are sampled points, $\Delta t_k$ are distances, $D(r_i)$ is ground truth depth, $\epsilon$ is a kernel parameter, and $\hat{\sigma}$ is a variance parameter [S5].
- **parameter**: $\epsilon(x)$: A kernel that integrates to one (a distribution) with a bounded domain parameterized by $\epsilon$ [S5].
- **pitfall**: The URF loss (Urban-NeRF) has no open-source implementation, so KL loss is selected as the representative for indirect supervision [S5].

### Geometry and Opacity Regularization
- **formula**: Sparsity loss: $L_S = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} O(i)$, where $N$ is number of rays intersecting the 3D box, encouraging sparse opacity to suppress floaters [S6]. Opacity loss: $L_O = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} [O(i) \cdot \log(O(i)) + (1 - O(i)) \cdot \log(1 - O(i))]$, encouraging opacity values to be 0 or 1 to avoid translucent effects [S6].

### Depth Filtering with RGB Confidence
- **definition**: Filters predicted depth maps by computing a per-pixel confidence metric based on the reconstruction error between predicted and ground truth RGB images [S7, unofficial].
- **step**: Load predicted RGBs and depths from NeRF results directory. Load ground truth RGBs from the data directory. Compute confidence map by taking 1 minus the mean absolute error between normalized predicted and ground truth RGBs across channels. Pass ground truth RGB, predicted depth, confidence map, and save path to a parallel processing pool for filtering [S7, unofficial].
- **parameter**: worker_num: Number of parallel workers for the multiprocessing pool, default 8 [S7, unofficial].

### Direct Depth Supervision
- **definition**: A training objective that directly compares the depth rendered by the NeRF with a ground truth depth prior using a pixel-wise loss function [S5].
- **step**: First sample a batch of $N_r$ rays, then compare the rendered depth and ground truth depth with different loss functions (MSE or L1) [S5].

### GeoAug
- **definition**: An approach that uses data augmentation by rendering new training images with new noisy camera poses using DSNeRF as a baseline and using depth as regularization [S8].

## Background
The challenge of shape-radiance ambiguity in NeRF, particularly with sparse views, led to the development of geometric regularization. Early works like DS-NeRF [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md] introduced sparse 3D keypoints from SfM to supervise the density field. Subsequent research expanded to include monocular depth priors [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md], structural consistency [9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md], and hierarchical consistency [S1]. The field has evolved from simple L2 depth losses to more sophisticated distributional alignments [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md] and robust losses handling noisy stereo data [S3].
